title: Louis Cottrell, the Magnolia Band, Freddie Keppard and popularity
summary: He played occasionally with Louis Cottrell and admired Freddie Keppard, popular in the Olympia band.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles

blocks.x: You say Louis Caput knows you, huh?

Yeah. You work with him, then? Yeah, I play with him on occasion, you see. In other words, now he's an older musician than I am, but he wasn't too old for me to play with. You know, what I mean is this, for instance, you lots younger than I am, but if you was a trumpet player and I'm a trumpet player and I need one, I get you, I mean afterwards you could say, well I play with people. Yeah, yeah. You know?
He used to work with Earl. Earl used to play with him.
Yeah, I played with Earl, huh? Yeah. That's before you done it.
Well, since you run out, do you ever play with the Magnolia Band? No, never did.

I knew of the Magnolia Band. I know Louis Caput was with him, I thought maybe that was the same. You didn't know Caput's brother. Freddie? Yeah. I knew him like this, to the public. You never met him. No. Somebody say that's Freddie Caput. And then I'd see him on different occasions and I'd recognize him, see. But for me to know him, I don't know him, but I knew Louis. Did you hear him play? Did you hear him play? Oh yeah, Freddie, yeah. Oh you did? Oh yeah, I know, I heard him play lots of times. And I thought he was a nice trumpet player.
What band did he play with? Oh, let's see if I could call the name of the band, Olympica, believe me.
You thought he was very good?
I thought he was very good.

Yeah. Oh yeah. You see, that was one of the things, you know, people did this. If a group of people recognize you as being able to do something, other people follow the group.
